series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #21 (the practice that feels best)
hook: The practice that feels best teaches you the least.

gate.goal_link: any learning goal (an exam, a language, an instrument) where practice in blocks feels like progress but does not transfer to the real test
gate.mechanism: interleaving: blocked practice gives high practice scores but poor delayed performance, because you never practise choosing the method; mixed practice feels worse and works better. Rohrer & Taylor 2007 (interleaved 63% vs blocked 20% a week later), said as 'about three times higher'
gate.universal: revising by doing many of the same exercise in a row

frame.want: Riya wants to pass her maths exam
frame.obstacle: blocked practice feels great, the mixed exam makes her blank
frame.fix: shuffle problem types every session; expect more mistakes

hooks_considered.line: The practice that feels best teaches you the least.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y, muted Y (63 vs 20 bars), sendable Y, payoff Y

hooks_considered.line: You knew how to solve it. You just didn't know which one.
Getting every practice problem right is a bad sign.
Studying one topic at a time is why you blank in exams.
Same hours of practice. Three times the score.
